claim_ceiling: This register defines model structures, external comparators, data requirements and matched evaluation rules. It is not an executable ecological model, raw-data analysis, calibrated pathway partition, or evidence that any candidate currently outperforms another. AFEX raw files remain un-ingested. Organic nutrient uptake and fungal carbon costs are not identified by current AFEX child records.

empirical_target.experiment: Central Amazon AFEX randomized complete-block factorial

model_structures.name: Treatment-only factorial baseline
model_structures.principal_failure_test: Does an apparent mediator model add any out-of-block predictive value beyond treatment and block?

model_structures.name: Direct uncolonised fine-root inorganic acquisition
plant_pathways: direct inorganic N uptake by uncolonised roots
direct inorganic P uptake by uncolonised roots
unobserved_requirements: soil inorganic nutrient concentrations by plot/depth are not in the admitted crosswalk yet
model_structures.principal_failure_test: Can direct-root-only acquisition explain P/cation interactions and later turnover without AM contribution?

model_structures.name: Direct root plus mycorrhizal inorganic acquisition
plant_pathways: direct inorganic uptake by uncolonised roots
model_structures.carbon_cost: explicit fungal carbon allocation required for predictive model; otherwise flag as omitted
support_limitations: no fungal nutrient-transfer flux is measured
model_structures.principal_failure_test: Does AM colonisation add held-out predictive skill beyond direct root traits, while respecting its 0-10 cm support?

model_structures.name: Three-pathway direct-root / mycorrhizal-inorganic / mycorrhizal-organic model
plant_pathways: direct inorganic nutrient uptake by uncolonised fine roots
indirect inorganic nutrient acquisition by mycorrhizal roots
model_structures.carbon_cost: substrate-carbon availability or fungal carbon allocation required

external_comparator.name: ELM-MYCI / ELMv2-SPRUCE
external_comparator.model_scope: boreal peatland; spruce, tamarack and shrubs; calibrated/evaluated with SPRUCE
external_comparator.limitation: not a tropical Amazon AFEX baseline; its peatland/mycorrhizal guild and soil organic matter assumptions must not be transplanted without adaptation

required_data: soil inorganic and organic N/P pools by depth
fungal carbon allocation or defensible constraint
support_limitations: AFEX crosswalk currently lacks plot-resolved organic N/P access flux
AM colonisation fraction alone does not identify organic nutrient acquisition
no AFEX fungal carbon allocation observation admitted
model_structures.principal_failure_test: Can the additional organic pathway be identified and validated on independent outcomes, or does it merely add unidentifiable parameters?
model_structures.status: external architecture comparator; AFEX organic pathway currently unidentifiable

model_structures.name: Mycorrhizal carbon-cost and soil C/N coupled model
plant_pathways: plant carbon allocation to roots and symbionts
fungal_pathways: fungal effects on decomposition and soil C/N
model_structures.carbon_cost: explicit carbon allocation to mycorrhizal fungi and trade-off with host productivity

external_comparator.name: Myco-CORPSE

papers.scope: ECM effects on soil C/N decomposition conditioned on fungal traits, climate and litter
modelled mycorrhizal carbon costs across >1,800 eastern US forest inventory plots

external_comparator.reported_model_result: study reports 16.0% of NPP allocated to ECM fungi versus 5.8% to AM fungi in its temperate-forest analysis
external_comparator.limitation: the model and empirical evaluation are not a matched tropical AM AFEX benchmark; use for process structure and cost accounting, not direct score comparison

required_data: fungal carbon allocation or tracer constraints
support_limitations: AFEX current child records do not identify fungal C cost
no AM hyphal production/turnover dataset admitted
model_structures.principal_failure_test: Does carbon-cost coupling improve held-out carbon and nutrient predictions without violating C budgets?

model_structures.name: Mycorrhizal-type hierarchical trait–function model
model_structures.carbon_cost: not necessarily explicit; cannot claim a process budget unless measured

external_comparator.name: Huang et al. 2026 mycorrhizal-explicit trait model
external_comparator.sample: 63 subtropical tree species with in-situ 15N tracer uptake
external_comparator.reported_comparison: mycorrhizal-explicit hierarchical model R²=0.37 vs root-only model R²=0.19
external_comparator.limitation: species-level inorganic N uptake in a different subtropical forest; not a direct AFEX turnover or plot-level benchmark

support_limitations: current AFEX root trait files are community-level plot means
mycorrhizal type is not currently crosswalked by species to the tree census
there is no 15N flux measurement in current AFEX register
model_structures.principal_failure_test: Does type-conditioned trait prediction improve independent species-level uptake prediction when species identity and functional type are truly observed?
model_structures.status: methodological comparator; AFEX species-level fit not presently supported

model_structures.name: No-mediation / parallel response model
plant_pathways: treatment affects root traits and turnover through separate or unmeasured processes
fit_targets: out-of-block prediction of later turnover from treatment only
model_structures.principal_failure_test: Do trait mediators improve held-out prediction after treatment, block, support and temporal alignment?

model_structures.name: Omitted common-cause / model-set inadequacy challenge
plant_pathways: registered model pathways plus a hidden or withheld driver
model_structures.principal_failure_test: Can the ensemble detect that every registered model is wrong in the same direction?
model_structures.status: synthetic open-world challenge; field measurements not yet registered/admitted

mandatory_rules: Do not compare R² values from different ecosystems, response variables, sampling units or validation splits as if they were one leaderboard.
Use plot as the AFEX treatment assignment unit; cores, roots, point subsamples and repeated campaigns are nested.
Keep the AFEX as-published analysis separate from any preregistered robustness analysis.
Treat 0-10 cm AM colonisation and 0-30 cm turnover as different supports.
Do not identify mycorrhizal organic nutrient acquisition from AM colonisation percentage alone.
Do not claim fungal carbon cost without direct data or a clearly qualified constraint and carbon budget.
Do not assume all AFEX plots contain the same tree mycorrhizal guild distribution without species-level evidence.
Keep an explicit no-mediation model and an omitted-mechanism model in every matched tournament.
A model with more pathways must beat simpler models on frozen held-out outcomes, not just in-sample fit.
Report complexity, runtime, parameter identifiability, data needs, posterior/predictive calibration and abstention alongside predictive skill.

proposed_benchmark_targets.support_refusal: 100% of unsupported species/depth/time joins rejected on frozen adversarial corpus
proposed_benchmark_targets.baseline_comparison: all mechanistic models compared with treatment-only, root-only and no-mediation baselines on identical held-out plots
proposed_benchmark_targets.added_value: mechanistic pathway family retained only if it improves proper score or decision loss with uncertainty on the paired improvement
proposed_benchmark_targets.identifiability: report which pathway fluxes are identifiable; do not infer pathway fractions from colonisation or trait correlations alone
proposed_benchmark_targets.open_world: detect at least one withheld common-cause or omitted-pathway synthetic challenge without falsely selecting a more complex registered model
proposed_benchmark_targets.efficiency: report CPU/memory/runtime and observation/assay cost per increment in out-of-block predictive skill
